the on-shell renormalization of chargino and/or neutralino masses is not stable if the mass of the wino is used as an input parameter.
the on-shell renormalization of chargino and (especially) neutralino masses in the MSSM is very sensitive to the choice of input states.

the question of which input parameters are most suitable for the on-shell renormalization of a chargino-neutralino mass matrix.
the choice of input masses in the on-shell renormalization of chargino and neutrailno masses in the MSSM and we show that the choice of the input masses is not unique.

the renormalization procedure of the MSSM is very delicate and requires a careful treatment of all possible renormalization conditions in all sectors of the model.

the renormalization procedure of the charginos and neutralinos should not be done in a scheme where the mass of a higgsino is used as an input, but rather in a scheme where all three input states are neutralinos.

the renormalization scheme of the MSSM chargino and the neutralino sector is very stable and robust against the choice of input masses.

the renormalization scheme should be carefully chosen in order to minimize the size of the corrections to the masses in the chargino/neutralino sector.
